key_insight: The classical 2-dimensional Weisfeiler-Leman algorithm stabilizes in linear time, with a worst-case bound of at most 5(n−1) rounds, closing much of the gap to the known Ω(n) lower bound.
engineering_relevance: This gives a sharper theoretical runtime guarantee for graph isomorphism pipelines and any downstream system that relies on WL-style refinement in algebraic graph analysis or ML.
method: Prove a global linear upper bound for the classical 2-WL refinement process.
Extend the argument to k-WL for all k≥3, yielding improved bounds of O(n^{k-1}/(k-2)! + n^{k-2}).
Generalize the proof to a broader class of tuple-coloring sequences where the bounds are near-tight.
evidence_signal: The paper’s evidence is theoretical: it derives new upper bounds and compares them against prior O(n log n) and Ω(n) results, rather than reporting experiments.
watch_item: The bound is asymptotic and worst-case; practical runtime can still depend heavily on graph structure, initialization, and implementation details.
paper_title: The Classical Weisfeiler-Leman Algorithm Stabilizes in $O(n)$ Rounds
